provenance.paper_title: MEM: Multi-Scale Embodied Memory for Vision Language Action Models

evidence.section: Full-paper method / memory representation and retrieval
evidence.paraphrase: A video encoder compresses dense recent observations for fine-grained control.

evidence.section: Full-paper method / memory representation and retrieval
evidence.paraphrase: A high-level policy maintains compressed language state for task progress over up to fifteen minutes.
The high-level policy autoregressively updates language memory during control. For MEM, this specifically supports a trained but frozen update module of short-horizon video memory.

evidence.section: Full paper: A. Multi-Scale Embodied Memory (MEM)
evidence.paraphrase: Long-horizon events are compressed into semantic task-state summaries. For MEM, this specifically supports episodic or hierarchical summarization of short-horizon video memory.

derived.hybrid_relation: Distinct operative representation paths are explicitly linked for downstream retrieval, reasoning, or control.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 2): During inference, the operative memory component (short-horizon video memory) changes through a trained but frozen update module, episodic or hierarchical summarization; the governing policy remains fixed, and any learning reported by the paper occurs before deployment. Training-time learning, when present, was not counted as T3.
